title: Each kind of block has a wrapping default and a toggle
body:
cmr's one wrapping control is the `width` given to `cmr::render` and `cmr::layout`. With it, cmr wraps paragraphs, headings, list items, quotes and table cells. It never wraps a code block. `code` in cmr's `lib.rs` emits one row per source line, highlighted line by line. coax keeps a code block or a table wider than the pane at its natural width (`kept_whole` in `ui.rs`), and you pan it sideways.

Panning suits code, where a line break changes meaning. It fails for text in a fence, such as a draft issue body. There the agent wraps lines by hand to avoid panning, so the text you approve differs in its line breaks from the text that gets filed.

## Proposal

- Each kind of block has a default, chosen in coax:

| block | default |
|---|---|
| code with a programming language | pan |
| `text` fence, or no language | wrap |
| table | pan |
| tool output | pan |

- The box's header row gets a `wrap|pan` chip. A click switches that block, and coax keeps the choice per block.
- cmr gains a way to wrap a code block's lines after highlighting, so a wrapped line keeps its colours. A wrapped row marks that it continues the line above it.

## Open

- The shape of the cmr change: a flag to `layout`, or a field on `Block::Code`. That needs a cmr issue once the shape is settled.
- Whether a person can change the defaults in `config.toml`.
- Which glyph marks a continuation row.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/bd10c4a0
notes.text: Header row design, shared with coax-06ff60 and coax-784c36 (Jack, 2026-11-10): a block's header row keeps `┌ lang` on the left and the copy glyph on the right. Toggles sit between them as dim words, with the active one in `accent`, as in `┌ markdown   render raw   wrap pan   ⧉`. A word shows only on blocks where it applies. The defaults stay as the issue's table has them, fixed in code with no `config.toml` setting for now. cmr's `Block::Code` gains a `wrap` flag that the parser sets to false and coax sets per block before layout. A wrapped row shows `┆` in the gutter in place of `│`.
